title: WHAT IF JOSEPH HOLDS A GRUDGE?

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Joseph's brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, 'What if Joseph holds a grudge against us and pays us back for all the wrongs we did to him?'" — Gen 50:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Seventeen years have passed. Seventeen years of Joseph feeding them, housing them, giving them the best land in Egypt, weeping over them, embracing them. And the moment their father dies, the old fear comes flooding back: what if he has been waiting all this time?

This is what unresolved guilt does. It cannot believe forgiveness is real. They have received kindness for nearly two decades and still assume there is a bill coming.

Many Christians live exactly here. We know the doctrine — Christ died for our sins, we are forgiven, there is no condemnation. And still, somewhere underneath, we are waiting for God to bring it up. We interpret every hard season as the payment finally arriving.

But God is not storing up a grudge against His children. Christ did not partially deal with your sin. Scripture says our transgressions have been removed as far as the east is from the west (Ps 103:12) and that God remembers our sins no more (Heb 8:12).

If God has forgiven you, He is not waiting for the right moment to raise it again. The brothers wasted seventeen years being afraid of a man who loved them. Do not do the same with your Father.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you half-expect God to bring up sins He has already forgiven?
2. Where does old guilt still shape how you relate to Him?
3. What would change if you truly believed you are fully forgiven?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are not holding a grudge against me. Help me stop waiting for a bill that Christ has already paid, and live as someone genuinely forgiven. Amen.
